issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name mismatch in the template prevents students from following the UML/specification exactly and may cause confusion or compilation errors if tests or instructions refer to emptyStock().
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(), so the template matches the UML and the solution and students can implement/compile code as described.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template implementation provides a method named clearInventory(). This naming mismatch refers to the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) and can confuse students who will look for emptyStock() as specified in the task and tests, increasing extraneous cognitive load and potentially causing failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem specification and the solution, or add a new emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory() so the template, tests, and problem statement use the same identifier.
